images.title: The remainder comes back
images.purpose: Show the long division of 10 by 3, where the remainder 1 appears at every step so the quotient 3.333... never ends.
images.composition: One short long division layout in the centre, with the four repeated remainders highlighted and one short note to the right; wide white margins.
exact_structure: A long division bracket with divisor 3 on the left, dividend 10.000 inside and quotient 3.333... above, digits aligned by place.

Working under the dividend, top to bottom, 4 identical steps: −9 under the 10, a line, the remainder 1; a 0 is brought down beside that 1 to make 10; then −9, a line, remainder 1; and so on, so −9 appears exactly 4 times and the remainder 1 appears exactly 4 times, the last one followed below by three small grey #6B7280 dots.
Subtracted rows −9 in teal #0072B2, with a thin grey #6B7280 line under each of the 4 subtracted rows.
Each of the 4 remainders 1 is circled in reddish purple #CC79A7.
To the right of the circled remainders, one reddish purple note: remainder 1 again.
rejection: the division drawn as ending with remainder 0
images.takeaway: When the same remainder comes back, the same step repeats, so 10 ÷ 3 = 3.333... never ends.
images.description: A long division of 10 ÷ 3 with quotient 3.333..., where each remainder is 1 and is circled in purple.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on 10 ÷ 3.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students what the next step would be after the last remainder 1.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the remainder 1 return in the layout is the whole idea of this concept.
